subject: Intermittent private deployment timeouts & retry amplification — TritonPay impact
messages:
From: ops@tritonpay.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s from private deployment - TritonPay

Prio team —

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx and 429 responses from the private Redwood deployment serving our auth/token route around 07:50 PDT. Volume is normal for the hour but error rate jumped to ~18% and many calls are timing out after 8s. Our retries are amplifying the issue on our side. Attaching short logs and a pcap.

What we have so far:
- Errors started at ~07:50 and are intermittent across instances
- Some requests succeed with ~900ms latency, others hit 5xx or 504 timeouts
- We have not rolled any config changes on our side

Please escalate — this impacts card authorizations and users are seeing failed payments.

— Alex Rivera
ops@tritonpay.com
TritonPay Operations

Attachments: tritonpay-logs-20270522.zip (zip), network-trace-20270522.pcap (pcap)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429s from private deployment - TritonPay

Marissa / Neha / Jonas — forwarding TritonPay ops. They report a sudden rise in 5xx/429s + timeouts on their private deployment (VPC-connected Dedicated). They attached logs and a pcap. They say retries are amplifying impact.

Quick ask: can infra/networking confirm whether there was any VPC peering churn, SNAT exhaustion, firewall rule changes, or DNS resolution delays in us-west-2 starting ~07:45-08:00 PDT? This is customer-impacting and TritonPay has asked for executive attention.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Triage: confirm if multiple nodes lost peering or if NAT ephemeral ports saturated
- If NAT/peering: open short failover to alternate egress or expand SNAT pool (if available)
- If DNS: point TritonPay to the regional fallback address and clear DNS caches where safe
- Exec: loop in sales leadership if we need to offer credits or commit a mitigation timeline

I can join in a call with TritonPay in 15.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429s from private deployment - TritonPay

On 22 May 2027 08:22, priyom_das@redwood.com wrote:
> Quick ask: can infra/networking confirm whether there was any VPC peering churn, SNAT exhaustion, firewall rule changes, or DNS resolution delays in us-west-2 starting ~07:45-08:00 PDT?

Summary from infra triage (first pass):
- VPC peering health: brief BGP flap observed between our peering router and TritonPay's edge at 07:48 for ~90s; routes re-advertised automatically
- NAT metrics: transient spike in ephemeral port usage on the dedicated SNAT gateway at the same timeframe (port reuse/translation fallbacks observed)
- Firewall policies: no recent policy changes; connection tracking table surged but rules were stable
- DNS: increased latency to internal resolver at 07:47, queries retried — likely tied to the peering flap affecting resolver reachability

Implications: the BGP flap likely caused a short window where some worker nodes couldn't reach TritonPay's VNIs reliably, leading to increased client-side retries and partial timeouts; SNAT exhaustion then amplified retries into additional connection failures.

Immediate mitigations we've applied:
- Expanded SNAT ephemeral port range temporarily for TritonPay's pool
- Added a short static route for TritonPay's CIDR to bypass the flaky peering hop while we confirm stability
- Restarted affected resolver daemons; cleared DNS cache on edge nodes serving that tenant

Requesting:
- Ops (Jonas): confirm whether peering provider has follow-up diagnostics and whether we should request TritonPay to establish a secondary peering or use a fallback interconnect
- Sales (Priyom): notify TritonPay we have an active mitigation and ask them to hold retries for 60s while we stabilize; offer a postmortem and credits if SLA breach confirmed

I'll keep the channel updated — planning a 10:00 PDT sync if needed.

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Eng Manager, Infra
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ops@tritonpay.com, network-lead@tritonpay.com
Date: 2027-05-24T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429s from private deployment - TritonPay

Following up with the consolidated findings and next steps after provider diagnostics: 

Provider feedback:
- Peering provider confirmed a control-plane transient caused route withdrawal at 07:48 due to a neighbor flapping on their edge; they fixed the neighbor at 07:50 and routes stabilized
- No intentional maintenance was scheduled

Final impact analysis (preliminary):
- Window of instability: 07:48–07:51 PDT
- Customer-facing error amplification due to SNAT ephemeral port pressure and retries: increased error surface through 08:10 as retries queued
- Estimated affected requests: ~12k requests, peak error rate ~18% for the window

Completed remediations:
- Permanently expanded SNAT pool for TritonPay tenant and applied rate-limited connection throttling to reduce retry amplification
- Added a persistent secondary static route for TritonPay to prefer a different peering path when available
- Implemented resolver health-check and automated local fallback to avoid single-resolver dependency

TritonPay ask and next steps:
- TritonPay acknowledged mitigation as of 09:00 PDT and is running a stress pass.
- Sales/CS (Priyom): recommend offering a one-month credit and a formal postmortem scheduled next week.
- Infra/Net (Marissa, Neha): follow up with peering provider for a root-cause writeup and implement BGP dampening rules on the affected edge.

I'll prepare a short postmortem doc and share the Drive link to the artifacts.

— Jonas Weber
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
